name: NCP4308DDR2G
title: NCP4308: synchronous rectifier controller for flyback and LLC supplies
summary: A secondary-side controller that drives a synchronous rectifier MOSFET in CCM, DCM or QR flyback and LLC converters, sensing the MOSFET's drain directly on a 150 V CS pin. It turns on at −75 mV and off at 0 mV, with 8 A sink and 4 A source drive clamped at 9.5 V (B, D, Q) or 4.7 V (A, C, suited to GaN). Resistors set the minimum on and off blanking times, and the Q version adds an adjustable maximum on-time that lets a QR primary run in CCM. NCP4308DDR2G is version D (4.45 V UVLO, 9.5 V clamp) in SOIC-8, the only order code still offered.

circuits.title: LLC converter with two synchronous rectifiers
circuits.description: A half-bridge LLC stage: M1 and M2, run by the LLC controller, drive the primary N1 of TR1 through the series capacitor C1. The secondary is two windings N2 and N3 joined at a centre tap that is the output. Each outer end goes through its own SR MOSFET (M3, M4) to the return, and each MOSFET has its own NCP4308: CS on the drain, GND on the source, DRV on the gate, VCC from the output with C3 or C4 from VCC to GND, and the two timing resistors from MIN_TON and MIN_TOFF to GND. C2 holds the output. Regulation goes back to the primary through the zener D1 and the optocoupler OK1.

parts.note: transformer; N1 primary (N1_1 dotted), N2 and N3 secondaries (N2_1, N3_1 dotted)

notes: M1 and M2 each have a diode from source to drain.
U1 GND and U2 GND each run to their own MOSFET's source.

circuits.title: DCM, CCM or QR flyback with secondary synchronous rectifier
circuits.description: A single-switch flyback. On the primary, M1 switches TR1 from the bulk rail, R2 senses its current for the flyback controller, R1, C2 and D3 clamp the drain, and the auxiliary winding feeds the controller's VCC through D4 into C3. On the secondary, the SR MOSFET M2 sits in the return leg. The NCP4308 takes VCC from the output with C4 to GND, senses M2's drain through R5 (the threshold-shift resistor), returns GND to M2's source, drives M2's gate, and has R3 and R4 as its MIN_TOFF and MIN_TON resistors. C5 holds the output; D5 and OK1 carry the feedback.

parts.note: transformer; P1/P2 primary (P2 dotted), S1/S2 secondary (S1 dotted), A1/A2 auxiliary (A1 dotted)

notes: U1 GND and C4 return to M2's source by their own trace.

circuits.title: Primary-side regulated flyback with secondary synchronous rectifier
circuits.description: A flyback regulated from the primary: the controller reads the auxiliary winding through the divider R3, R4 (filtered by C4) on its ZCD pin, and its COMP pin carries C5 and the series R5, C6 to ground. M1 switches TR1, R2 senses current, R1, C2 and D3 clamp the drain, and D4 with C3 feeds the controller's VCC from the auxiliary winding. There is no optocoupler. The secondary is the same SR stage as the plain flyback: M2 in the return leg, the NCP4308 on the output with C7 across VCC and GND, R8 in series with CS, R7 and R6 on MIN_TOFF and MIN_TON. C10 holds the output.

parts.note: transformer; P1/P2 primary (P2 dotted), S1/S2 secondary (S1 dotted), A1/A2 auxiliary (A1 dotted)

circuits.title: QR flyback forced into CCM at heavy load by MAX_TON (NCP4308Q)
circuits.description: A quasi-resonant flyback with the Q version on the secondary. The SR stage is as in the plain flyback (M3 in the return leg, R8 in series with CS, R9 and R10 on MIN_TOFF and MIN_TON, C5 across VCC and GND), and the divider R11, R12 from the output sets the MAX_TON pin. DRV also drives the small pulse transformer TR2 through C6. On the primary, TR2's winding drives the gate of M2 through R7, clamped by the zener D5; M2 pulls the controller's ZCD node to ground, so the end of SR conduction at tMAX_TON acts as a ZCD event for the controller and lets the primary turn on in CCM. The ZCD node also takes the auxiliary winding through R3 and R4 (D4 across R4), with R6 and C3 to ground. M1 is driven through R1 with D1 across it, R2 senses current, R5, C2 and D2 clamp the drain, and D3 with C4 feeds VCC. Feedback goes through the zener D6 and OK1.

circuits.title: Modulating the minimum on-time with an NPN transistor
circuits.description: RMIN_TON sets the base blanking time from MIN_TON to GND. A second resistor RMIN_TON_2 from the same pin goes to ground through the NPN Q1; the voltage on Q1's base switches or throttles that path, drawing extra current from the pin and so changing the blanking time. The control signal can come from load current, the feedback voltage or another quantity. MIN_TOFF can be modulated the same way.

circuits.title: Setting and modulating the maximum on-time (NCP4308Q)
circuits.description: RMAX_TON from MAX_TON to GND carries the pin's 100 µA source current and so sets the MAX_TON voltage and the maximum on-time. The optional RA from VOUT makes the maximum on-time depend on VOUT, so it can be longer when VOUT is low during hard overload or start-up.

operation.text: The NCP4308 runs a synchronous rectifier MOSFET on the secondary of a switch-mode supply, either on its own or alongside a primary controller. It decides from the MOSFET's drain-source voltage alone when to switch on and off, so it works in CCM, DCM and QR flyback and in LLC converters. A 0 mV turn-off threshold and an 8 A sink driver let the MOSFET conduct for nearly the whole of the secondary current pulse. The 5 V clamp versions (A, C) are offered for driving GaN transistors.
Notebook adapters, compact AC/DC chargers for phones, LCD TV supplies and any switch-mode supply that needs high efficiency.

VCC runs from about 4 V (A, D, Q) or 8 V (B, C) to 35 V, so the chip can sit straight on the output of most adapters. Below VCCOFF the chip draws 75 µA typ. After VCC first rises past VCCON there is a start-up delay of 75 µs typ.

When VCC is missing, drain swings coupled through the MOSFET's gate-drain capacitance would lift the gate. The chip uses that pulse on DRV to power its sink transistor, holding the gate low (not to zero) until VCC is present.

When the secondary voltage reverses, the MOSFET's body diode conducts and the drain falls to about −1 V. CS sources 100 µA; once the CS voltage is below VTH_CS_ON (−75 mV typ) the driver turns the MOSFET on. A minimum on-time, set by RMIN_TON, then blanks the turn-off comparator so ringing cannot switch the MOSFET off early.

The MOSFET turns off when CS rises above VTH_CS_OFF (−0.5 mV typ), less any drop across the optional RSHIFT_CS. The turn-off current therefore depends on the MOSFET's RDS(on). The 100 µA bias through RSHIFT_CS raises the turn-on, turn-off and reset thresholds referred to the drain; its effect on turn-off matters most. Shorting RSHIFT_CS is recommended. With a 1 mΩ MOSFET, a −10 mV threshold would leave 10 A flowing at turn-off, while 0 mV turns off at 0 A.

A minimum off-time starts when CS rises above VTH_CS_RESET (0.5 V typ) and must run out before another drive pulse. If the drain rings back below VTH_CS_RESET while it runs, the timer resets, and it restarts once the voltage rises again, so ringing after turn-off cannot retrigger the driver. The total blanking stretches with the ringing.

After start-up the driver stays off until one full minimum off-time has passed with CS above VTH_CS_RESET. Each dip of CS below VTH_CS_RESET during that wait restarts the timer; only after a complete period is the output enabled.

MIN_TON and MIN_TOFF are each set by a resistor to GND, independent of VCC: the pin holds a reference, and a scaled copy of the resistor current charges an internal capacitor. Roughly 1 µs per 10 kΩ. The shortest times are clamped inside to 55 ns on and 245 ns off, so a pin shorted to GND is safe. The times can be modulated with extra parts, such as an NPN that adds a second resistor in parallel.

The Q version adds MAX_TON: a resistor to GND sets a maximum conduction time, 4.8 µs typ at 3 V on the pin and 48 µs typ at 0.3 V. When it runs out the MOSFET turns off before the secondary current reaches zero, and the rest flows in the body diode. DRV, coupled to the primary side by a little pulse transformer, acts as an early ZCD event, so a QR controller can turn on in CCM at heavy load without cross conduction, keeping the minimum switching frequency up and allowing a smaller core. A resistor RA from VOUT lengthens the maximum on-time when the output is low, during overload or start-up.

The turn-off comparator measures CS against the GND pin, and with a 1 mΩ MOSFET each 1 mV of error shifts the turn-off current by 1 A, so milliohms or nanohenries in the sense path matter. Use a Kelvin connection: GND to the MOSFET source solder point, CS to the drain solder point. Lead inductance in a leaded package (TO220) adds a voltage proportional to di/dt that pulls CS towards zero while current still flows, turning the MOSFET off early; the loss grows with lower RDS(on) and higher frequency. Keep leads as short as possible; a leadless SMT MOSFET makes the shift negligible. Two MOSFETs in parallel need a symmetric Kelvin connection. VCC is decoupled by 100 nF and 1 µF capacitors in parallel, returned to the GND pin.

The SR MOSFET always switches at zero voltage: its body diode conducts before turn-on, and turn-off begins before the drain voltage rises. So the gate-drain capacitance adds no Miller charge and the gate load is Ciss at the clamp voltage (Qg_ZVS), which differs from the total gate charge most MOSFET data sheets give for hard switching and may need measuring, since it is non-linear. The steps: find Cg_ZVS, compute the gate drive loss for the chosen 5 V or 10 V clamp, add the IC's own consumption, then the die temperature. With no external gate resistor and a small internal gate resistance, nearly all the gate drive loss lands in the driver. PCB layout changes the real thermal resistance.
